summary: This plan constructs signed Reidemeister torsion for symplectic local systems, its extension over normal rings and its identification with the étale second Chern transgression. It imports the existing graded determinant and spinor norm theories. A characteristic-free circle proof, normalized specialization, an explicit Gaussian witness and the arithmetic transfer argument connect the topological theorem to finite-field K-theory.

nodes.title: Cochain, shift, dual and cone conventions
nodes.statement: Use bounded cochain complexes of finite projective R-modules, R commutative and 2 invertible. R[k] is in degree −k; C[1]^q=C^{q+1} with differential −d. nodes.title: Subdivision and simple cellular invariance
nodes.statement: For compact smooth manifolds with compatible finite triangulations, the determinant quasi-isomorphism induced by an elementary cellular expansion/collapse with volume-preserving even-rank coefficients carries e to e. Hence the scalar torsion square class is independent of triangulation, using common subdivisions and elementary simple changes. An arbitrary quasi-isomorphism alone does not preserve a chosen cellular volume.
proofSteps: Compute the two-term acyclic cell pair of an elementary expansion: its attaching matrix is a signed monodromy matrix of determinant one in even rank.
Apply determinant multiplicativity to its cancellation.
Use compatible subdivisions and simple comparison maps for smooth finite triangulations; transport Poincaré duality with them.

nodes.title: Reidemeister torsion modulo squares
nodes.statement: Let X be a closed smooth oriented (2m+1)-manifold and K a field of characteristic ≠2. Let ρ have even rank and a perfect locally constant (−1)^m-symmetric pairing: symplectic if m is odd; orthogonal with a specified standard self-dual volume if m is even. Transport e_X through det C≃det H*(X;ρ). The upper cohomology truncation H^{>m} is Lagrangian for Poincaré duality. Define RT(X,ρ)=e_X/ν_{H^{>m}} in Kˣ/Kˣ². No acyclicity is required.
proofSteps: Construct the cohomological root class using the induced perfect pairing.
Use cellular invariance and pairing-compatible comparison maps to show independence of choices.
In the acyclic case the denominator is the canonical acyclic determinant class.

For S¹ over Q, Gram matrix I₂ and rotation A=[[0,−1],[1,0]], RT=[2].

nodes.title: Three volumes on an algebraic boundary
nodes.statement: Let C be a strongly even skew-symmetric dimension-4j complex over K, j≥1, and D=∂alg C. On det D compare a from C∨[−4j]⊂D, b from σ≥2j D, and c from upper cohomology via det D≃det H*D. Then a=b=(−1)^r c, with r≡(χ(C)+χ₁/₂(D))/2 (mod 2). In particular χ₁/₂(D) is even. Only the parity of r is asserted by this formula; the actual acyclic middle rank is 2r after the splitting.
proofSteps: Shift by 2j−1 to the strict symmetric dimension-1 case. Compare a and b degree by degree using strongly even Lagrangians.
Apply strict-splitting: Q and its dual give the same classes, while the acyclic alternating block of rank 2r has square determinant and reverse-wedge scalar (−1)^r.

Equivalently [(−1)^{χ₁/₂/2}]RT(M,ρ)=1. The dimension parameter j is independent of half the coefficient rank.
proofSteps: Use the relative pairing on N and the boundary-cone comparison. All cellular term ranks are even.
Factor e_N into relative and boundary generators. Use duality-volume to compute the cone-Lagrangian class on the boundary.

nodes.title: Even strict models
nodes.statement: For a symmetric dimension-1 finite projective Poincaré complex over R with 2 invertible and even fibre semicharacteristic on a connected neighbourhood, Zariski locally there is a pairing-compatible strict free model whose every term has even rank, after adjoining canonically trivialized symmetric contractible summands. The determinant comparison preserves any given determinant volume.
proofSteps: First strictify locally. Work from the outermost degrees inward: a contractible free rank-one pair together with its shifted dual adjusts two adjacent term parities and their reflected partners.
Continue until only degrees 0,1 can have odd rank. Their parity is the lower-half rank sum, equal to χ≤0 modulo two, hence is even.
Use the canonical acyclic determinant trivializations to transport the volume. This stabilization argument is part of the theorem, not an assumed property of all strict models.

nodes.title: Torsion over normal rings

Classify the resulting determinant line with square trivialization by a μ₂-torsor.

nodes.statement: For a closed smooth oriented three-manifold with a symplectic finite projective R-local system, R normal integral with 2 invertible, define N_R=[(−1)^{χ₁/₂(generic)/2}]RT_R. nodes.title: The circle formula in odd characteristic
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic ≠2, V have even dimension and nondegenerate symmetric form of square unsigned discriminant, choose a standard self-dual volume, and let A∈SO(V). Then h=dim V^{A=1} is even and (−1)^{h/2}RT(S¹,A)=θ(A). No semisimplicity, lifting or characteristic-zero assumption is imposed.
proofSteps: Split V=V₋⊥U at the generalized −1 block. Both blocks have even dimension, and 1+A is invertible on U.
On V₋ the circle is acyclic and det(1−A)=2^{dim V₋}, a square. On U use strict-circle-calculation, retaining disc(B|U).

Since the total discriminant is square, disc(B|U)=disc(B|V₋) modulo squares. Multiply the even-block determinant classes and apply the minus-one Zassenhaus formula. This proves the finite-characteristic case without Jacobson–Morozov or a logarithm.
acceptance: Over Q with B=I₂ and A=1, raw RT=[−1], h=2 and normalized RT=θ(1)=1.
Over F₃ take B hyperbolic of dimension four and A=diag(U,U⁻ᵀ), U=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Then h=2, θ(A)=1 and raw RT=[−1]; this detects both the sign and a characteristic-zero-only proof.
For an even-dimensional square-discriminant form and A=−1, h=0 and both sides equal 1.

nodes.title: The orthogonal cohomology of a surface
nodes.statement: For a closed smooth oriented genus-g surface Σ, symplectic rank-2r local system over K of characteristic ≠2 and H⁰(Σ;ρ)=0, the cup-product/fibre pairing makes V=H¹(Σ;ρ) nondegenerate symmetric, of dimension 4r(g−1) and square unsigned discriminant. A chosen symplectic intertwiner for an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism induces T∈SO(V).
proofSteps: Poincaré duality gives H²=0 and the symmetric perfect H¹ pairing. Cellular Euler characteristic gives the dimension, divisible by four.

The cellular volume and its duality comparison have scalar (−1)^{rχ(Σ)}=1. Transport through det C≃(det H¹)⁻¹; the reverse-wedge correction in dimension divisible by four is one. Hence the Gram determinant is square.

The diffeomorphism and chosen symplectic intertwiner preserve the cellular volume. Since only H¹ remains, their determinant on H¹ is one. This is a determinant argument in any odd characteristic, rather than a lift of the representation.

nodes.statement: With Σ,ρ as above, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism f and a specified symplectic intertwiner f*ρ≃ρ define ρ_f on M_f and T on H¹(Σ;ρ). For every field of characteristic ≠2, h=dim ker(1−T)=dim H¹(M_f;ρ_f) is even and (−1)^{h/2}RT(M_f,ρ_f)=θ(T). Also θ(T)=det(1−T|V₊⊥)disc(V₊), where V₊ is the generalized 1-eigenspace, not merely the fixed space.
proofSteps: Use the two-cylinder Mayer–Vietoris model or the Wang triangle C*(M_f)→V[−1]→(1−T)V[−1].
Track the cellular numerator through the cylinder decompositions; identical unknown transport determinants occur twice and cancel modulo squares. Track Poincaré pairings with the fixed shift.
Apply the circle formula to V and T, then the equivalent plus-one Zassenhaus formula. The Wang sequence gives H⁰(M_f)=0 and H¹(M_f)=ker(1−T).

nodes.title: A genus-two cocycle model
nodes.statement: For π=⟨a₁,b₁,a₂,b₂ | [a₁,b₁][a₂,b₂]=1⟩ and a representation on V with ρ(b₁)−1 invertible, evaluate a crossed homomorphism by φ(gh)=ρ(g)φ(h)+φ(g) and φ(g⁻¹)=−ρ(g)⁻¹φ(g). The single relator determines φ(a₁) from the other three values. Thus H¹(Σ;ρ)=coker(ι:V→V³), ι(v)=((b₁−1)v,(a₂−1)v,(b₂−1)v). An automorphism t and intertwiner M induce T̃(φ)=M⁻¹φ∘t, descending to T on this cokernel. If 1−M⁻¹ is invertible, det(1−T)=det(1−T̃)/det(1−M⁻¹).
proofSteps: Use cellular degree-one cochains of the surface presentation and expand the relator by the crossed-homomorphism rule; its a₁ coefficient is 1−ρ(a₁b₁a₁⁻¹), invertible by hypothesis.
The principal crossed homomorphisms give exactly ι, which is injective because b₁−1 is.

Check T̃ι=ιM⁻¹, then apply determinant multiplicativity to the short exact sequence. Acyclicity of 1−T is unnecessary for the polynomial identity, but is needed to use a nonzero determinant as torsion.

The cocycle φ_v(g)=ρ(g)v−v is sent by T̃ to φ_{M⁻¹v}.
For rank-two coefficients satisfying the hypothesis, dim V³/ι(V)=4, matching the genus-two Euler calculation.

The intertwiner is M=[[0,−1],[1,0]]. Then char_T(x)=x⁴+1, det(1−T̃)=4, det(1−M⁻¹)=2, h=0 and N=RT=[2]=[i]≠1 in Q(i)ˣ/Q(i)ˣ². Compute determinants 4/2 and 8/2. The identity 2=(1−i)²i identifies the first square class; if (a+bi)²=i with rational a,b, then a=±b and 2a²=±1, impossible.

nodes.title: Good finite fields
nodes.statement: An odd finite field k is good if N_k=c_et on B_r(k)=H₃(Sp_{2r}(k);ℤ)/2 for every r≥1. The finite-rank comparison makes these groups cyclic of order two and stabilization an isomorphism. Thus it suffices at one rank to find x with normalized torsion N_k(x)≠1. A nonsquare raw RT witness is sufficient only after also accounting for its semicharacteristic half-sign.
proofSteps: Define the predicate by equality of homomorphisms.
Use the finite-field étale isomorphism and rank stabilization to characterize goodness by a nonzero normalized value.

A constant rank-two system on S³ over F₃ has raw nonsquare RT=[−1] but normalized value 1, so it cannot be the nonzero witness.
A nonzero witness at Sp₂ remains nonzero under every standard stabilization.

nodes.title: The transfer lemma
nodes.statement: Let S be a normal integral finite-type Z[1/2]-algebra with maps to odd finite fields k₀,k₁. If a=c_et(x)∈H¹(S,μ₂) specializes nontrivially at both maps, then k₀ is good if and only if k₁ is good.
proofSteps: Put b=N_S(x). At every finite closed-point specialization with a=0, the finite-field Chern isomorphism forces x=0 and then b=0.
Quadratic-cover Frobenius detection implies b lies in the F₂-span of a: otherwise there is a closed point where a=0 but b≠0.
If k₀ is good, b specializes there to the nonzero a, so b=a globally. Its nonzero specialization at k₁ proves goodness there; reverse the roles for the converse.

nodes.title: Weighted density and controlling extensions
nodes.statement: For a set P of finite places of a number field L set w_P(X)=X⁻¹Σ_{v∈P,Nv≤X}log Nv. Record both lower and upper limits. A controlling pair (E/L,S) consists of a finite Galois extension and a nonempty conjugacy-invariant subset S⊂Gal(E/L) such that the bad unramified places with Frobenius in S have upper weighted density zero, equivalently w_bad(X)→0. A place is good when its odd residue field is good. Finite exceptional places and residue degree greater than one have weight tending to zero.
proofSteps: Define the counting functions and exceptional-set condition with an actual zero limit.
Import weighted Chebotarev for conjugacy subsets and the prime-power/residue-degree tail estimates from the current upstream roadmap.
Allow an empty controlling subset only as a formal input to the compositum operation when its output subset is nonempty.
acceptance: The empty subset is not a controlling witness for a field extension.
Places of residue degree at least two have weight O(X⁻¹/² log X), hence limit zero.
A finite union of upper-density-zero sets has upper density zero; two sets of lower density zero need not have a zero-density union.

nodes.title: Controlling extensions and intermediate fields
nodes.statement: Let E/L be finite Galois, L⊂M⊂E, S_M⊂Gal(E/M) nonempty and invariant under conjugation by Gal(E/M), and S_L its conjugacy closure in Gal(E/L). Then (E/L,S_L) is controlling if and only if (E/M,S_M) is controlling.

Use the Frobenius orbit criterion: a class in the conjugacy closure meets Gal(E/M) exactly when there is a residue-degree-one place of M with that Frobenius class.
Goodness agrees because the residue fields then agree. Bound the number of primes lying over a prime by [M:L] and preserve the zero upper-density condition in both directions.

Any nonidentity element of W* detects at least one basis class. The dim W≥1 condition ensures the controlling subset is nonempty.

One may choose a sufficiently large rational prime r≡1+h (mod 2h), unramified in E and K, and take the degree-h cyclic subextension of K(ζ_r)/K.
proofSteps: Use the coprime congruence class 1+h modulo 2h to choose r avoiding finitely many primes.
The cyclotomic extension is totally ramified at r, while E and K are unramified there; obtain the degree and disjointness.
Because (r−1)/h is odd, complex conjugation has nontrivial image in the cyclic quotient, so every real embedding becomes complex.

nodes.title: The cubic density improvement
nodes.statement: Given a controlling (E/K,S) containing a fixed controlling quadratic subextension, put δ=1−|S|/|Gal(E/K)|. If 0<δ≤1/2, construct a controlling (E′/K,S′), E⊂E′, with δ′≤δ−δ³/16. Iteration gives lower weighted density one for good places of K.
proofSteps: Take the least even h≥4 with 2^{−h/4}≤δ/2 and a disjoint totally imaginary cyclic L/K of degree h. The controlling quadratic class remains nonsquare in L.

Choose a finite Galois-stable liftable subspace W over L of dimension N≥h/2, by taking the orbit span of finitely many independent classes. Let L̃=L(√W), so Gal(L̃/L)=W*. Descend its nonidentity controlling subset to K and combine it with E.

Write Γ=Gal(EL̃/K). The projection Γ→Gal(E/K)×Gal(L/K) is surjective, but no surjection to Gal(E/K)×Gal(L̃/K) is assumed. The fraction outside S and over identity in Gal(L/K) is δ/h; at most 1/(h2^N) also maps to identity in Gal(L̃/K). New good fraction is at least (δ−2^{−N})/h.
Minimality of h gives h⁻¹≥δ²/8 and 2^{−N}≤δ/2; hence the cubic decrease. A positive limiting δ contradicts the recurrence.

nodes.title: Lifting finite-field homology through Witt vectors
nodes.statement: For every odd finite field k, r≥1 and x∈H₃(Sp_{2r}(k);ℤ)/2, there is a normal integral finite-type Z[1/2]-domain S⊂W(k), a reduction map S→k and a class x_S∈H₃(Sp_{2r}(S);ℤ)/2 mapping to x. No integral surjectivity of a Sylow inclusion is claimed.
proofSteps: For a Sylow 2-subgroup Q, transfer followed by inclusion is multiplication by the odd index, hence inclusion H₃(Q;ℤ)/2→H₃(Sp(k);ℤ)/2 is surjective.

Take the finite-type subring of W(k) generated by lifted matrix coefficients, form coefficients, inverses and 1/2. Normalize in its fraction field: finite-type Z-algebras are excellent, so normalization is finite; W(k) is integrally closed, so reduction extends. The finite bar cycle descends.

Every field of characteristic ≠2 is a filtered union of finite-type domains with 2 invertible and their finite normalizations inside the field.

Integral bar cycles and their relations use finitely many group elements, and finite étale torsors and Chern constructions descend along filtered colimits. Transport equality to all fields without assuming a particular field embeds in characteristic zero.

nodes.title: The topological torsion theorem
nodes.statement: Let M be a closed smooth oriented three-manifold and ρ a symplectic rank-2r local system over any field K with characteristic ≠2. Then χ₁/₂(M,ρ)=dim H⁰−dim H¹ is even and [(−1)^{χ₁/₂/2}]RT(M,ρ)=⟨ρ*c_et,[M]⟩ in Kˣ/Kˣ². The evaluation is on the integral fundamental cycle reduced modulo two.
proofSteps: Apply the transformation equality to the image of the oriented fundamental class in integral group homology modulo two.
Use normalized-transformation.manifold and Kummer comparison to identify the two sides.

nodes.title: The mapping-class spinor identity
nodes.statement: For any closed smooth oriented surface Σ, field K of characteristic ≠2, symplectic local system ρ with H⁰(Σ;ρ)=0, orientation-preserving diffeomorphism f and specified symplectic isomorphism f*ρ≃ρ, let T on H¹ and ρ_f on M_f be induced by that choice. Then θ(T)=⟨ρ_f*c_et,[M_f]⟩. This includes all odd finite coefficient fields.
proofSteps: The Wang sequence gives χ₁/₂(M_f)=−h, h=dim ker(1−T), so its half-sign agrees with (−1)^{h/2}.
Combine the all-odd mapping-torus formula with the topological theorem. Keep the chosen intertwiner as part of the data: f*ρ≃ρ without a choice does not specify T or ρ_f.

nodes.title: The real Chern component and the metaplectic cover
nodes.statement: For G=Sp_{2r}(R) considered as a discrete group, r≥1, identify the degree-(2,2) component c₂₂ of the standard representation’s mod-two étale c₂ with the pullback of its topological metaplectic double-cover class in H²(G;F₂). The latter is the reduction modulo two of the integral class of the universal covering group, whose central kernel is ℤ. Its coefficient Bockstein to H³(G;F₂) therefore vanishes.
proofSteps: Import the universal Chern class and its real comparison, with the standard-representation normalization.
Use the universal symplectic covering group with kernel ℤ; push out by ℤ→ℤ/4→ℤ/2. This lifts the metaplectic extension to a ℤ/4-extension.

Apply the exact coefficient sequence to conclude its Bockstein is zero, also after forgetting topology. The real Chern/metaplectic identification is a supplier request, not a consequence of the integral H₃/2 comparison.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the real degree-three Chern component
nodes.statement: For G=Sp_{2r}(R) discrete, c₃₁:H₃(G;F₂)→H¹_et(R,F₂) is zero on the full mod-two homology group, for every r≥1. In particular its restriction to integral H₃(G;ℤ)/2 is zero.
proofSteps: Use the coefficient Bockstein compatibility of the universal étale c₂: after evaluating cycles, β_et c₃₁ is obtained from the group Bockstein of c₂₂.
That group Bockstein is zero by metaplectic-component.

For Gal(C/R)=C₂, the connecting map β_et:H¹(R,F₂)→H²(R,F₂) is an isomorphism, as the generator squares nontrivially. Hence c₃₁=0. Do not infer this stronger domain statement solely from integral H₃ modulo two.
